subject: Follow-up: Model fit + Redwood-verified benchmarks for PayFront
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@payfront.com>, Maya Lee <maya.lee@payfront.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Model fit + Redwood-verified benchmarks for PayFront

Thanks both for your time today — really helpful call. Quick recap + next steps based on what we discussed: 

Summary of requirements
- Primary workload: payment reconciliation / customer support summarization + high-quality entity extraction from receipts (short text, lots of numeric noise)
- Peak concurrency target: ~120 TPS during batch settlement windows (short bursts), steady-state 8-12 TPS
- Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for real-time chat flows; background batch jobs can be relaxed
- Data constraints: PII present, prefer VPC/private deployment for production

Redwood recommendation (shortlist)
- For accuracy-cost tradeoff: redwood-llama-13b-q4 (recommended quantized variant) — best balance for extraction tasks
- For lower-latency/high-throughput routing: redwood-deploy-7b-int8 for live chat; route batch jobs to 13b quant when throughput is less latency-sensitive
- Eval suggestion: run your sample traffic through both variants (7b int8 + 13b q4) using our prompt set (attached) to measure exact quality delta and token cost

Performance and benchmarks
- Shared Redwood-verified performance profiles link below — includes TPS baselines and latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95) for each model under different batch sizes and sequence lengths
- Key numbers to check: p95 latency at 16-token response and 64-token response; TPS measured with continuous batching enabled

Next steps (proposed)
1) You share a 24–72 hour sample of anonymized traffic (schema/1k-5k messages) — we can run a payfront-specific eval and return a one-page fit summary
2) Redwood runs a quick canary benchmark (we can do this on Dedicated or in a VPC staging environment) — typical turnaround 2–3 business days once sample is received
3) Sync to review results and pick the deployment path (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private)

Links and attachments
- Redwood benchmark dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/payfront-2026
- Prompt set (attached): prompt_sets_payfront_v1.zip
- Redwood performance PDF (attached): redwood_model_profiles_20260327.pdf

I cc'd Marissa (solutions) and Dylan (SRE) to help scope the canary and the deployment options. If that plan looks good, can you share the sample by COB Monday PST? If not, tell me the earliest window that works for you and we’ll align.

Thanks again,
Alex
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---

From: Samir Gupta <samir@payfront.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit + Redwood-verified benchmarks for PayFront

Alex — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency: when you say p95 <= 200ms, is that for single-request latency (no batching) or for a configured batching window? We need to understand live chat SLA (sub-200ms) vs batch windows.
2) Throughput: our bursts could hit ~120 TPS sustained for 2–5 minute windows. Do the TPS numbers in the dashboard reflect sustained bursts or averaged over longer tests?
3) Can you run the eval on our sample? We attached a small anonymized sample (payfront_sample_traffic.csv) — please let me know if the schema is sufficient.

Also looping in Maya (Ops) — she’ll coordinate any NDA/procurement asks.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Engineering | PayFront Inc.
samir@payfront.com

On a side note, curious about any guidance you have on autoscaling policies for Dedicated vs Hosted in the context of these bursts.

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@payfront.com>, Maya Lee <maya.lee@payfront.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit + Redwood-verified benchmarks for PayFront

Thanks Samir — appreciated. We got the sample and it’s sufficient to run an initial eval. Answers inline: 

Latency definition
- The p95 <= 200ms I referenced was measured with continuous batching enabled at small batch sizes (typically 2–8 requests per batch) on our dedicated runtime; single-request (no batching) p95 will be higher, and depends on sequence length and kernel selection. The Redwood dashboard shows both batching and no-batching curves — look for the "p95 (batch=4)" metric.

TPS measurement
- Our TPS numbers on the dashboard include both sustained and burst tests. For burst windows we run step tests (2–10 minute sustained load) and report peak sustained TPS. The PayFront dashboard view defaults to "sustained-5m" by legend. For your 2–5 minute bursts, the sustained-5m numbers are most relevant.

Canary eval
- We’ll run the sample through the two recommended configs (redwood-deploy-7b-int8 and redwood-llama-13b-q4). Deliverables: per-prompt accuracy (precision/recall where applicable), token-cost estimate, and a one-pager with recommended routing policy (live vs batch). Expected delivery: 48–72 hours after we start the canary.

Autoscaling guidance (short)
- Hosted: automatic, but can see variability during large simultaneous customer events — we recommend a buffer and soft-SLA for pilot
- Dedicated: you can configure headroom and burst capacity; Dedicated + small autoscale window (90–120s) gives predictable p95s for short bursts

Attachments and links
- Attached: redwood_model_profiles_20260327.pdf (one-page perf summary), prompt_sets_payfront_v1.zip
- Dashboard (payfront view): https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/payfront-2026
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/pf-2026-0421

Marissa / Dylan — can we kick off the canary on Tuesday morning PST? If you want, I can share temporary dataset access and a runbook.

Alex
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
